subject: tmbstan not working at all for me?

messages.author: f5b13b580eb160db
messages.subject: tmbstan not working at all for me?
parts:
Hello,

My apologies in advance if this question doesn't have sufficient information to be answer-able; I'll happily provide anything else I can if that's the case. In short, I can't get the tmbstan package to work at all. I have a TMB function (let's call it "func" here) that, although being quite complex and somewhat slow, works and gives me good MLE's for the data I provide it. No errors or issues. But when I run

tmbstan(func)

I get a "Fatal R Error" and am forced to restart RStudio entirely. I found this a bit odd so I wanted to make sure the simple example provided by the tmbstan package would work. Turns out, that didn't evaluate either - same fatal error. I've attached a screenshot of my console output taken seconds before the fatal error (it's named Picture1.png; sorry if the quality is not fantastic but hopefully it's readable). 

I'm running R 4.2.3 on Windows using the RStudio IDE (version 2023.03). As far as I know these are the most up-to-date versions of R and RStudio. I tried re-installing the TMB, rstan, and tmbstan packages - but still no luck. I'm guessing this is probably something happening in my local directory / namespace (maybe there's some function that's being over-written by another package? maybe a C++ library of some sort that I'm missing somehow?) so I've posted it here rather than as a Github issue, but if others find the same issue on their devices, maybe it's not just me.

Any kind of help is greatly appreciated. Thanks!
Peter R. Thompson

messages.author: 361e593259030741
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] tmbstan not working at all for me?
parts:
Hi. 
One of the most likely possibilities might lie in an index problem.  The set of "TMB - R -  R studio" in the Windows machine is too sensitive to an error in indexing, I observe.   What I mean with an "indexing" error is a mismatch between your intending to point an element in an array and the corresponding element.   Whenever running into the mismatch problem, the R studio is forced to terminate.  This is very annoying, and thus a few friends, who use TMB, recommend we should use Linux or Mac for TMB instead of Windows.  Anyhow returning back to my main point, please check whether, in your loop (e.g., for, while, etc.) in your CPP file, your indices were correct.  Recall that the TMB index starts at zero (i.e., i =0, not i=1).   Your attachment does not show your CPP file, and thus I am not sure though that my guess is right. 
Saang-Yoon

messages.author: 258b98968d0ad8b9
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] tmbstan not working at all for me?
parts:
Peter,

Obviously, if example(tmbstan) crashes your R session there's something seriously wrong. I don't think the problem is in tmbstan though given that it works on all CRAN's 13 test systems. They all run 'example(tmbstan)' when checking the package:

https://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_results_tmbstan.html

On the other hand, if tmbstan is the only package causing problems you should perhaps file a bug report. Don't forget to include sessionInfo().
